Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

isoniche 1.1.0

New maintainer: Itai Granot. Author order is now Granot, Dubiner, Belmaker; Itai Granot and Shahar Dubiner contributed equally.

Bug fixes

These change results relative to 1.0.0.

  • The n-dimensional isodar (fit_isodars(dim = "ndim")) is now a line (the first principal axis), not a hyperplane (the smallest eigenvector) combined with “closest to equal allocation”. The old approach biased niche breadth toward generalism.
  • Inverse-variance weights (weights = "1/var") were applied twice (effectively 1 / sd^4). They are now 1 / (sd^2 (1 + slope^2)), applied once.
  • isoderr(output = "SE") divided the bootstrap standard deviation by sqrt(n_boot). The bootstrap SD is itself the standard error, so “SD” and “SE” now both return it.
  • fit_isodars() no longer recurses forever when an isodar has a negative slope and a negative intercept.
  • Density-independent niche breadth (iai(abundances = NULL)) is now evaluated at the first integer total with at least min_occupancy (default 1) individual in every habitat. Previously the threshold was > 1e-9 individuals. If no total qualifies, one row of NA is returned.
  • hab_cols = NULL silently used every column of data. Now hab_cols (or n_habitats) is required.

New features

  • A new user-facing layer works on one or many species at once:
    • fit_isodars() accepts long-format data (one row per species x site x habitat, columns named by species, site, habitat, abundance and optionally effort) and returns one fit per species (isodar_fits). Counts are converted to densities per reference_effort (default: the median effort). The wide-format interface is unchanged.
    • niche_breadth() returns, per species, density-independent and density-dependent niche breadth with site-bootstrap confidence intervals, the spillover abundance (the total at which the least-favoured used habitat reaches one individual), preference-reversal abundances, abandoned habitats and diagnostic flags as columns. Printing it gives one summary line and the unit of abundance. Density-dependent niche breadth is by default the limit at infinite abundance (dependent_at = "asymptote"), computed directly. The flags include a test of whether isodar intercepts differ from sampling noise (multinomial null model, as in the paper). With seed, each species gets its own random streams, and the user’s random-number state is restored afterwards.
    • summary() of a niche_breadth() result counts the species with estimates and without warning flags, gives quartiles of the estimates and, for each flag raised, how many species raised it, what it means and what to do about it.
    • iai_curve() and its plot() method give niche breadth as a function of total abundance, with bootstrap bands, each species’ density-independent value and asymptote, preference reversals, and the totals at which two species’ curves cross. The curve is drawn thinner beyond the largest observed site total, the x-axis gives the unit of abundance, and the legend avoids the curves. plot() of a niche_breadth() result plots its curves.
    • community_to_long() converts a community matrix (samples x species) and a table of sample attributes into the long format, pooling samples from the same site and habitat and summing their effort.
    • check_coverage() summarises sampling coverage per species and habitat; group_sites() merges nearby sites (complete linkage on great-circle distance, summing counts and efforts); radius_sensitivity() shows how results change with the grouping radius.
    • fit_isodars() and niche_breadth() warn when the data have an effort column that is not used, and reference_effort without an effort column is an error.
  • simulate_isodars() simulates any number of habitats (slopes, intercepts), optional missing habitats (p_missing) and long-format output; the three-habitat default gives the same numbers as before.
  • New data set moorea_fish: reef fishes of Moorea in three habitats (the paper’s Table S2).
  • New vignettes: vignette("isoniche") (get started), vignette("data-preparation"), vignette("diagnostics") and vignette("method"); citation("isoniche"); a pkgdown website.
  • Habitats a species never uses are handled. fit_isodars() (and isoderr()) gain absent = "auto", which declares a habitat absent when the species has no more than absent_max_count (default 0) records in it across at least absent_min_sites (default 5) sites where it was present in another habitat. Absent habitats are excluded from the isodar fit, fixed at 0, and counted as 0 in the inequality, so they lower niche breadth. Previously such habitats broke the fit and iai() returned NA. Habitats with no records but fewer informative sites give a warning and are kept. Use absent = "none" for the old behaviour or name habitats directly. A species that uses a single habitat has niche breadth 0. isoderr() decides the absent set once, on the full data. Results for species that use every habitat are unchanged.
  • Scaled niche breadth is kept within [0, 1] (rounding error could give values such as -1e-16).
  • New pairwise_niche() summarises pairwise isodars into niche breadth indices (paper, revised Appendix S1). By default (scale = "log") the indices do not depend on which habitat of each pair is on the x-axis: slope deviations are log(b)^2 and intercept deviations use the perpendicular distance of the isodar from the origin, abs(a) / sqrt(1 + b^2); it returns the inverse root-mean-square deviations and the weighted means of abs(log(b)) and of that distance, with optional weights ("1/var", the inverse perpendicular residual variance, or numeric). Isodars with non-positive slopes are left out of the slope indices with a warning. $cycles checks consistency: the product of the slopes around each cycle of three habitats, which should be 1, flagged beyond cycle_tolerance. scale = "linear" gives the earlier indices (mean intercept and slope, deviations (b - 1)^2 and a^2); log_slope is a deprecated alias.
  • Pairwise isodars use every site where both habitats of a pair were recorded, so sites that lack some habitats still contribute.
  • fit_isodars(dim = "ndim", ndim_method = "latent") estimates the line from incomplete sites (every site with at least two habitats) as a one-factor model fitted with glmmTMB, and checks that the habitats are connected through shared sites. ndim_method = "auto" picks "pca" when all sites are complete and "latent" otherwise.
  • fit_isodars() returns classed tibbles (isodars_pairwise, isodar_line).
  • iai() allocates abundance among habitats by weighted least squares on the pairwise isodar equations, constrained to the total and to non-negative abundances, solved exactly by an active-set method. (Setting negative habitats to 0 and re-solving, as first implemented, could miss the optimum when a habitat dropped early should have been kept. For the 325 species of moorea_fish, no density-independent value or spillover abundance changes, and no value in the paper’s reference table; density-dependent niche breadth rises slightly for 3 species at the asymptote, by at most 0.014, and for 1 species at a total of 1000, by 0.002.) When the isodars do not determine the allocation (for example, a habitat without records was kept), iai() says so instead of failing with “singular matrix”.
  • isoderr(output = "CI") returns percentile bootstrap intervals.
  • iai() gives an informative error when abundances contains NA, non-finite or negative values.
  • Unit tests cover the paper’s reference values, a simulation with a known answer, each bug fix above, input validation and the latent method.
